_comment: Single source of truth for every football data source in the project. Read by the backend (routes/datasets.py) and by scripts/upload_datasets.py. local_path is relative to the Research root on the machine that holds the raw data. Raw data is NOT stored in git; it lives in S3 under datasets/<id>/.

sources.name: PFF FC World Cup 2022
sources.description: All 64 World Cup 2022 matches. Broadcast tracking (29.97fps, 22 players + ball, speed per player) plus analyst-tagged events, synced. Real touch counts and graded first touches. Main source for the process stats.
sources.license: Terms not checked yet (public Google Drive release)
sources.notes: TRACKING DATA stays bz2-compressed (about 1.2GB unzipped per match, never load whole into memory). 'Event Data/March 14, 2025/' is an older superseded release and is skipped. '_cache' is derived and skipped.

sources.name: DFL / Bundesliga integrated dataset (Bassek 2025)
sources.description: 7 matches (2 Bundesliga, 5 2. Bundesliga) with in-stadium optical tracking at 25Hz and official DFL events. Nothing estimated. Accuracy check for PFF methods.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0, credit Bassek, Rein, Weber & Memmert (Scientific Data 12:195, 2025)
sources.notes: Events and positions need an algorithmic sync (ELASTIC / DataBallPy).

sources.name: Metrica Sports sample data
sources.description: 3 anonymised matches, 25Hz tracking plus basic events synced by frame number. Sandbox for building and debugging methods.
sources.license: No formal licence; acknowledge Metrica Sports
sources.local_path: FOOTBALL LEARNING - Classes/UPPSALA COURSE/Chapter 4 (see class site)/Tracking data/sample-data-master

sources.name: Friends of Tracking code (Laurie Shaw)
sources.description: Metrica IO, smoothed player velocities (Savitzky-Golay, 12 m/s cap), pitch control (Spearman), EPV and plotting. Reusable for speed and time/space stats.
sources.license: Check the Friends of Tracking repo before redistributing
sources.local_path: FOOTBALL LEARNING - Classes/UPPSALA COURSE/Chapter 4 (see class site)/Friends of Tracking code
sources.notes: Stored in S3 for reference. Adapt the code before using it on PFF or DFL formats.

sources.name: StatsBomb / Hudl open data
sources.description: Event data plus 360 freeze frames (no tracking). 67 competition-seasons, about 3,200 matches, 210 with 360. Best event data; real Miscontrol events.
sources.license: Research / academic use only (no commercial use). Credit StatsBomb.
sources.notes: 6,676 small JSON files. Older copy of the live repo (new seasons exist upstream). Euro 2020 is also in the app's existing flattened CSVs at the bucket root.

sources.name: StatsBomb PL 2015/16 (Swish extract)
sources.description: All 380 PL 15/16 matches, trimmed to 50 columns (type, under_pressure, duration, locations, pass and carry details). League-wide baseline for miscontrols and dispossessions.
sources.license: StatsBomb research use. Derived from the Swish assessment file.
sources.notes: Drops xG, first_time, freeze frames and pass flags. Use the raw StatsBomb files for the full version.

sources.name: SkillCorner open data (2019/20, old release)
sources.description: 9 title-race matches, 10fps broadcast tracking of visible players only, no events. Two clasicos can be hand-synced with StatsBomb events.
sources.notes: StatsBomb match ids for the clasicos: 303596 and 303470.

sources.name: SkillCorner open data (2024/25 A-League)
sources.description: 20 A-League matches: 10fps broadcast tracking, dynamic events (possessions, pressing, off-ball runs, passing options), phases of play. Built-in pressure and time-to-impact metrics.
sources.license: MIT, credit SkillCorner (software licence, email before monetising)
sources.notes: NOT DOWNLOADED yet. Clone with git lfs (tracking is about 89MB per match), then add a local_path and upload.

sources.name: Wyscout public dataset (Pappalardo et al. 2019)
sources.description: About 1,941 matches, 3.25M events: 2017/18 big-5 leagues, World Cup 2018, Euro 2016. Includes Acceleration and Touch sub-events. Coarser than StatsBomb.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0, credit Pappalardo et al., Scientific Data 6:236 (2019)
sources.notes: Use players.json from this copy for player names.

sources.name: WhoScored / Opta PL 2020/21
sources.description: Full PL 2020/21 season of Opta events as served by WhoScored (about 600k rows, isTouch flag and full qualifier lists).
sources.notes: Served by the private app by choice; flagged private_only in case that changes.

sources.name: openplay (WhoScored / Opta, Bair 2026)
sources.description: 41.6M events across 125 competition-season parquet files: big-5 leagues 2014/15 to 2025/26, CL, EL, World Cups, Euros, Copa, AFCON, Nations League. Plus matches, players, teams, lineups, shots (xG), player and team match stats.
sources.license: Author says CC BY 4.0 (credit 'openplay (Noah Bair)') but events were scraped from WhoScored. Private research only.
sources.notes: Hashes in SHA256SUMS.txt. Only PL 14/15 has been inspected. Served by the private app by choice; flagged private_only in case that changes.

sources.name: ELASTIC event-tracking sync tool
sources.description: Syncs event data to tracking data and finds pass receive moments. Ships hand-labelled true timestamps for 3 DFL matches. Needed for the DFL dataset.
sources.notes: Clone it (git clone) rather than uploading. Not stored in S3.
